title: Federated Physics-Informed Thermal Field Prediction Across Unseen Geometries in Distributed Additive Manufacturing
abstract: arXiv:2611.17794v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In additive manufacturing (AM), each change in part geometry requires a new thermal simulation, which makes design evaluation over many candidates costly. Geometry-aware models reduce this cost by predicting thermal fields on unseen parts with a single learned model, but they assume that diverse geometries are available centrally. This assumption is restrictive when each manufacturing site holds only a limited set of proprietary part designs that it cannot share. We propose Fed-PIGANO, a federated framework that trains physics-informed geometry-aware neural operator (PI-GANO) models at individual sites and aggregates their geometry encoders and prediction networks without sharing part geometries. We evaluate the framework on a 2D steady-state thermal benchmark for metal AM, with geometries from five polygonal families distributed across three sites under four scenarios that range from identical to strongly different family compositions.

translated_title: 分布式增材制造中跨未见几何形状的联邦物理信息热场预测
translated_abstract: 在增材制造（AM）中，每次零件几何形状的改变都需要进行新的热仿真，这使得对大量候选设计的评估成本高昂。几何感知模型可以通过单一训练好的模型在未见过的零件上预测热场，从而降低这一成本，但这类模型假设多样化的几何形状数据可以集中获取。当每个制造站点仅持有有限的、无法共享的专有零件设计时，这一假设便具有很强的局限性。我们提出了Fed-PIGANO，一个联邦学习框架，它在各个站点独立训练物理信息几何感知神经算子（PI-GANO）模型，并在不共享零件几何数据的情况下聚合各站点的几何编码器和预测网络。我们在金属增材制造的二维稳态热基准上对该框架进行了评估，几何形状来自五个多边形族，分布于三个站点，并在从族组成相同到差异显著的四种场景下进行了测试。
tldr: 该论文提出Fed-PIGANO联邦学习框架，使各制造站点能够在不共享专有零件几何数据的前提下联合训练物理信息几何感知神经算子模型，从而在分布式增材制造中实现对未见几何形状的热场预测。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Fed-PIGANO, a federated learning framework that enables distributed manufacturing sites to jointly train physics-informed geometry-aware neural operator models without sharing proprietary part geometries, achieving thermal field prediction across unseen geometries in distributed additive manufacturing.
